options: Code that runs automatically in response to a DML event on a specific sObject
A public method you call from a Lightning component
A scheduled batch job that runs nightly
A validation rule configured declaratively in Setup
questions.explain: A trigger is Apex code bound to one sObject that the platform invokes automatically on insert, update, delete, or undelete — you never call it directly.

questions.q: In `trigger AccountTrigger on Account (before insert, before update) { }`, how many sObjects can this one trigger be bound to?
options: As many as are listed in the event list
Exactly one — Account
Zero, until an event fires
Two, since there are two events listed
questions.explain: A trigger is always scoped to exactly one sObject, regardless of how many events it lists.

questions.q: Which trigger event does NOT exist in Apex?
options: after undelete
before delete
before undelete
after insert
questions.explain: There is no before undelete event — undelete only fires after, since a record restored from the Recycle Bin has nothing to validate beforehand.

questions.q: Once you save a new trigger in your org, when does it start running?
options: Only after you deploy it to production
Only after you manually flip an 'Enable' toggle
Immediately, on any matching DML, unless explicitly deactivated
Only when called from another Apex class
questions.explain: Triggers are active the moment they're saved, with no separate enable step — unlike many other automation tools.

questions.q: What invokes a trigger — the UI, the API, Data Loader, or another Apex class performing DML?
options: Only the UI can trigger it
Only the API can trigger it
Only another Apex class can trigger it
Any of them — a trigger fires on the DML event regardless of its source
questions.explain: A trigger reacts to the DML event itself, not to where it came from, so UI saves, API calls, Data Loader jobs, Flows, and other Apex code can all fire it.
